SM-GM-I1-the-cited-demonstration-node-is.gap:
THE EXACT HOLE FI-06 NAMED, MADE EXECUTABLE. `demonstrate.py:165-176` compares
only the observed exit code, and pytest exits 0 for a passing run AND for a run
whose items were all collected and then skipped. So a demonstration whose cited
node stops actually asserting anything keeps reporting `ok`, and the registry's
count keeps reading as coverage.

TWO SKIP SHAPES, SEEDED SEPARATELY AND ON PURPOSE. This row uses `pytestmark`,
which collects the items and skips them -- pytest exits 0. `SM-GM-I6` uses
`allow_module_level=True`, which collects nothing -- pytest exits 5. If the
first survives and the second dies, then FI-06's sentence is right about the
mechanism and imprecise about its reach, and SM-03 needs to know which because
one shape is a real blind spot and the other is not. That distinction was NOT
in the finding; it came out of a synthetic exercise of this runner before any
real mutant was measured, and it is written down here rather than discovered
later next to a number.

Note this is also invisible to a full-suite run: a skip is not a failure, so
`pytest tests -q` stays green either way.
